next_steps: Read-only gate: do not split or edit yet; first collect the monolith Skill path, current trigger/body responsibilities, real usage scenes, consumers, and concrete failure samples showing where product/development/test/delivery responsibilities collide.

Run a routing/分流 capability check before choosing owners: identify whether the requested two-Skill split overlaps existing domain Skills such as product-manager, tech-lead, delivery-owner, tester, or skill-creator, and build an ability matrix for responsibilities, triggers, inputs, outputs, and handoff boundaries.

Apply skill-refiner intake standards before strategy confirmation: define scene facts / real usage scene and quality standard / quality-dimensions for the optimized Skill system, then ask the user to confirm the target split boundary and routing rules.

If the confirmed work is only new trigger/description wording or a net-new Skill definition, route that portion to skill-creator; if the issue is responsibility conflict, trigger ambiguity, or lifecycle/routing behavior in an existing Skill system, keep ownership with skill-refiner.
risk_notes: Splitting a monolith before proving boundaries can create two vague Skills instead of one vague Skill; the core risk is routing ambiguity, not file structure.
Existing capability reuse is unproven, so creating new Skills now would be premature and may duplicate adjacent domain Skills.
Consumers matter: downstream agents/users need deterministic routing cues and handoff contracts, otherwise the split increases orchestration cost.
No completion evidence is being evaluated here; this is an intake/routing dry run, so completion_evidence_blocked is not appropriate.
reason_summary: 根据 skill-refiner 分工，这不是立即创建两个新 Skill 的场景，而是既有 Skill 系统的职责边界与分流问题。下一步应由 skill-refiner 做只读 intake：确认真实场景、痛点样本、消费者、质量维度和现有能力矩阵，再让用户确认拆分策略；若最终只剩新 Skill 文案/触发器创建，再转 skill-creator。
